sources.title: SagarVidya/distilbert-emotion-model_v4 · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: This model is fine-tuned on the DistilBERT base model (distilbert-base-uncased) to classify text into five distinct emotions. It is trained on the Emotion Dataset using the Hugging Face Trainer API, leveraging the powerful DistilBERT architecture.

sources.title: How to Fine-Tune DistilBERT for Emotion Classification
sources.snippet: Radar chart of fine-tuned DistilBERT model. Image by author. Before fine-tuning, the pre-trained model performed poorly on our dataset, because it hasn't seen the specific emotion labels before. It was essentially guessing at random, as reflected in an AUC score of 0.5 that indicates no better than chance. sources.title: Okoth67/emotion-distilbert-finetune - GitHub
sources.snippet: 🧠 Emotion Classification with DistilBERT This project demonstrates how to fine-tune the distilbert-base-uncased transformer model from Hugging Face on the emotion dataset. The goal is to classify text into one of six human emotions: sadness, joy, love, anger, fear, and surprise.

sources.title: tharUmesh/emotion-classification-distilbert - GitHub
sources.snippet: Emotion Classification with DistilBERT This repository contains a Jupyter Notebook that fine-tunes a DistilBERT model to classify emotions in tweets using the dair-ai/emotion dataset. The project demonstrates a complete NLP pipeline, including data preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and inference.
